turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I focused on candidates lying in the high-zT composition neighborhoods in the training set. The strongest training regions were:

- Pb–Te–S / Pb–Te–Se-rich compositions, with zT often >1.8 and up to ~2.26.
- Cu–Se-rich compositions, with zT around ~1.45–1.74.
- Sn–Ni–Zr–Hf compositions, with zT around ~1.2–1.35.
- Some Co/Sn/Zr/Bi and Sb/Fe/Nb/Ti regions, generally lower than the above.

The best pool candidates by similarity to those high-performing neighborhoods are:

1. c052 — Pb–Te–S composition close to the highest Pb–Te–S training examples.
2. c054 — Cu–Se composition close to high Cu–Se training examples.
3. c012 — Pb–Se composition near high Pb–Se training examples.
4. c078 — Sn–Ni–Zr–Hf composition very close to high Sn–Ni–Zr–Hf examples.
5. c063 — another Cu–Se composition near the high Cu–Se region.

Final: c052, c054, c012, c078, c063
